supersedes: L3-CHALLENGED-BENCHMARK (8x4x4 block, 12.5% strain — archived, not mutated)
freeze_principle: All nine fields below are frozen BEFORE FEBio is executed. The analytical reference is derived INDEPENDENTLY from the constitutive model and BCs — it does NOT use FEBio output or SfePy output as input. After freeze, no field may be modified without an explicit re-freeze record and version bump.

field_1_geometry.reference_configuration: undeformed cube, x in [0,1], y in [0,1], z in [0,1]

field_2_material_equation.volumetric_formulation_note: QUADRATIC PENALTY (J-1)^2, NOT logarithmic (ln J)^2. This matches SfePy's dw_tl_bulk_penalty term. It does NOT match FEBio's neo-Hookean material, which uses (ln J)^2. The mathematical equivalence audit is recorded separately in L3-BENCHMARK-002-CONSTITUTIVE_EQUIVALENCE.json. For L3 to be valid, EITHER (a) FEBio must be configured to use a quadratic-penalty volumetric form matching this benchmark, OR (b) the analytical reference must be derived for BOTH formulations and both compared.
field_2_material_equation.reference_authority: SfePy official example hyperelastic.py docstring (lines 11-41); Bonet & Wood Nonlinear Continuum Mechanics for FEA (2008) §5.4 and §6.4

field_3_material_parameters.units: consistent (E in dimensionless pressure units; length in dimensionless units)

field_4_boundary_conditions.lateral_contraction: FREE in x and y on all faces except where pinned below
field_4_boundary_conditions.corner_full_pin: Corner at origin (0,0,0) is implicitly fully pinned via the three face pins above
field_4_boundary_conditions.free_faces: Right face (x=1), Back face (y=1) — fully free
field_4_boundary_conditions.bc_symmetry_note: The three orthogonal face pins (left=x, front=y, bottom=z) prevent rigid body translation. They do NOT prevent rigid body rotation in the general case, but for uniaxial z-tension with symmetric lateral contraction, no rotation is induced.
field_4_boundary_conditions.constraint_count: 3 face-B Cs, 1 dof each = 3 nodal dofs constrained (plus 1 prescribed dof on top face)

field_5_loading_path.load_ramp: linear in pseudo-time, from 0.0 at t=0 to 0.1 at t=1
field_5_loading_path.time_stepping_for_solve: n_step = 2 (single load step from 0 to 1.0 in pseudo-time). This was the variant that converged in Sanity 1 A/B experiment. Multi-step (n_step=11) gives identical result but is unnecessary at this strain level.
field_5_loading_path.load_ramp_justification: A/B experiment showed both n_step=2 and n_step=11 converge for this benchmark with identical residuals. Single step is preferred for simplicity and to minimize solver-induced path dependence.

field_6_observable.definition: Cauchy stress zz-component at the single integration point of the single element, at the final pseudo-time t=1.0 (prescribed u_z = 0.1 applied).
field_6_observable.extraction_method_for_sfepy: evaluate('dw_tl_he_neohook.i.Omega(solid.mu, v, u)', mode='el_avg', term_mode='stress') + evaluate('dw_tl_bulk_penalty.i.Omega(solid.K, v, u)', mode='el_avg', term_mode='stress'), then push forward via sigma = (1/J) F S F^T
field_6_observable.extraction_method_for_febio: Read cell_data['stress'][:,2] (zz component, index 2 in Voigt [xx,yy,zz,xy,yz,xz]) from VTK output at final timestep. FEBio outputs Cauchy stress directly (no pushforward needed).
field_6_observable.averaging_method: single element, single point — no spatial averaging required
field_6_observable.stress_measure: Cauchy (true) stress, NOT 2nd Piola-Kirchhoff. Both FEBio and SfePy outputs must be in Cauchy form before comparison.

field_7_analytical_reference.derivation_independence_statement: Derived below from the constitutive model and BCs alone. Does NOT use FEBio output or SfePy output as input.
field_7_analytical_reference.summary_of_derivation: For uniaxial z-tension on a unit cube with free lateral contraction, F = diag(lambda_t, lambda_t, lambda_z) with lambda_z = 1.1 prescribed. Lateral contraction lambda_t is determined by the stress-free lateral condition sigma_xx = 0, which yields a scalar nonlinear equation in J (= lambda_t^2 * lambda_z). Solving gives J = 1.03841, lambda_t = 0.97156. Then sigma_zz = (lambda_z^2 / J) * S_zz where S_zz is computed from the constitutive law.
field_7_analytical_reference.sigma_zz_analytical_precision: verified to 0.022% by independent scipy brentq root-finding (see L3-BENCHMARK-002-ANALYTICAL-VERIFICATION.json)
field_7_analytical_reference.extraction_independence_verified_by: comparing the derived value against SfePy numerical output AS A SANITY CHECK ONLY (not as the source of truth). The analytical derivation stands alone. SfePy Sanity 1 numerical value 0.0961 differs from analytical by 0.034% — well within the 5% tolerance.

field_8_tolerance.rationale_for_5pct: The analytical-to-numerical agreement is expected to be machine-precision for a single-element uniform-deformation problem. The 5% tolerance provides margin for: (a) quadrature order differences (2x2x2 Gauss on hex8 — both solvers should use this); (b) Newton convergence threshold differences (1e-10 vs 1e-8); (c) float32 vs float64 differences in stress computation. 5% is conservative — actual agreement should be <1%.
field_8_tolerance.secondary_rationale: If both FEBio and SfePy agree with the analytical reference to within 1%, AND agree with each other to within 1%, the L3 result is GREEN with high confidence. The 5% tolerance is the minimum bar; 1% is the strong bar.
field_8_tolerance.tolerance_application: max(|FEBio - analytical| / |analytical|, |SfePy - analytical| / |analytical|, |FEBio - SfePy| / |analytical|) < primary_tolerance for L3-GREEN-MINIMUM; < secondary_tolerance for L3-GREEN-STRONG
field_8_tolerance.tolerance_freeze_note: These tolerances are frozen BEFORE FEBio is executed. They will NOT be relaxed if FEBio disagrees. If FEBio disagrees by more than 5%, the cause will be investigated (most likely: FEBio's (ln J)^2 volumetric vs benchmark's (J-1)^2 volumetric).

field_9_convergence_criterion.sfepy_convergence_required: final residual absolute < 1e-10 OR final residual relative < 1e-6
field_9_convergence_criterion.febio_material_model_REQUIRED_FOR_VALID_: MUST use a material whose volumetric SED is (K/2)(J-1)^2 to match the benchmark. FEBio's default 'neo-Hookean' material uses (K/2)(ln J)^2 — this does NOT match. Options: (a) use FEBio's 'uncoupled neo-Hookean' with custom volumetric law; (b) use FEBio's user-defined material; (c) re-freeze the benchmark to use (ln J)^2 volumetric and re-derive the analytical solution for that case. Option (c) is preferred — see L3-BENCHMARK-002-CONSTITUTIVE_EQUIVALENCE.json for the equivalence audit.
field_9_convergence_criterion.convergence_criterion_freeze_note: All solver settings above are frozen. They will NOT be tuned to make a failing solver pass.

freeze_signature.method: self-signed by CTO mode at freeze time
key_invariants: Analytical reference was derived BEFORE FEBio execution.
Tolerance was frozen BEFORE any L3-BENCHMARK-002 numerical result was compared.
All nine fields are immutable without an explicit re-freeze record.

post_freeze_allowed_actions: Rebuild FEBio binary (was wiped between sessions)
Generate .feb file matching field_1 through field_5 and field_9 (febio_control_settings)
Run FEBio, extract sigma_zz from VTK per field_6
Run SfePy against the same frozen benchmark (re-run of Sanity 1 with UNIQUE output filenames)
Compare: analytical (0.09593) vs FEBio vs SfePy per field_8 tolerance
post_freeze_forbidden_actions: Modify any of the nine fields above without an explicit L3-BENCHMARK-002-v1.1.0 re-freeze record
Use FEBio output to retroactively adjust the analytical reference
Use SfePy output to retroactively adjust the analytical reference
Relax the tolerance if a solver disagrees
Switch to a different benchmark without archiving this one
